title: WebSockets
subtitle: Persistent full-duplex bi-directional TCP channels vs Short Polling, Long Polling, and Server-Sent Events (SSE).
keyTakeaways: WebSockets start as a standard HTTP/1.1 request with `Connection: Upgrade` and `Upgrade: websocket` headers, then hijack the underlying TCP socket for persistent full-duplex framing.
Because WebSockets are stateful, horizontal scaling requires a Pub/Sub backplane (like Redis Pub/Sub or Kafka) or consistent-hash routing so User A on Gateway 1 can message User B on Gateway 2.

Do not default to WebSockets when communication is strictly one-way (Server -> Client): Server-Sent Events (SSE) over HTTP/2 is simpler, stateless-friendly, and handles automatic reconnection natively.

sections.heading: 1. Architectural Fundamentals & Core Mechanics
sections.body: Standard HTTP is client-initiated: the server cannot push new data to the browser unprompted. Historically, engineers worked around this with **Short Polling** (client requests every 2 seconds, wasteful headers and empty responses) or **Long Polling** (server holds the HTTP request open until data arrives or a 30s timeout hits, then client immediately reconnects). **Server-Sent Events (SSE)** provides a standardized unidirectional stream (`text/event-stream`) from server to client over standard HTTP. **WebSockets (`ws://` / `wss://`)** upgrade the HTTP connection into a persistent, low-overhead (2-byte frame header), bi-directional binary/text channel.
bullets: **Core Architectural Principle**: WebSockets start as a standard HTTP/1.1 request with `Connection: Upgrade` and `Upgrade: websocket` headers, then hijack the underlying TCP socket for persistent full-duplex framing.

**Problem Space & Invariants**: Because WebSockets are stateful, horizontal scaling requires a Pub/Sub backplane (like Redis Pub/Sub or Kafka) or consistent-hash routing so User A on Gateway 1 can message User B on Gateway 2.
**System Boundary**: Operates across client network dispatch, gateway queuing, thread execution pools, and persistent storage I/O.

sections.heading: 2. Architectural Patterns & Implementation Topologies
sections.body: Distributed architectures apply specific implementation patterns and topologies for WebSockets:
bullets: **WebSockets (Full-Duplex Persistent Socket)**: Provides true bi-directional sub-millisecond framing (2-10 byte overhead), supports binary and text, ideal for high-frequency client-to-server-to-client loops. Best suited for Multiplayer browser games, collaborative whiteboards (Figma/Miro), live chat (Slack/WhatsApp), and financial order books.

**Server-Sent Events (SSE) / Long Polling**: Provides works natively over standard http/2 (multiplexed streams), built-in browser `eventsource` auto-reconnect with `last-event-id`, plays nicely with standard proxies. Best suited for AI LLM token streaming (ChatGPT), live sports score tickers, stock price dashboards, and notification feeds.
HTTP Upgrade Handshake: Uses `Sec-WebSocket-Key` and returns `HTTP/1.1 101 Switching Protocols`, ensuring compatibility with port 80/443 firewalls.

Heartbeats (Ping/Pong Frames): Intermediate NAT routers and AWS ALBs drop idle TCP connections after 60 seconds; WebSocket servers must send periodic `PING` frames (e.g., every 25s) to keep connections alive and detect zombie disconnects.

Thundering Herd on Restart: If a gateway node holding 100,000 connections crashes, all 100k clients will attempt to reconnect and re-authenticate simultaneously: clients MUST use randomized exponential backoff + jitter.
Load Balancing Metric: Never load-balance WebSocket gateways by 'Requests Per Second': balance by **Least Active Connections**.

sections.heading: 3. Production Strengths: Where & How to Apply
sections.body: Production deployments apply WebSockets across targeted operational scenarios:
bullets: **Where to Use: High-Impact Scenarios**: Optimal for Multiplayer browser games, collaborative whiteboards (Figma/Miro), live chat (Slack/WhatsApp), and financial order books, suited for environments requiring True bi-directional sub-millisecond framing (2-10 byte overhead), supports binary and text, ideal for high-frequency client-to-server-to-client loops.

**Where to Use: High-Throughput Scenarios**: Recommended for AI LLM token streaming (ChatGPT), live sports score tickers, stock price dashboards, and notification feeds, where Works natively over standard HTTP/2 (multiplexed streams), built-in browser `EventSource` auto-reconnect with `Last-Event-ID`, plays nicely with standard proxies.

**How to Use: Engineering Implementation**: Operating millions of persistent WebSockets introduces operational hazards that stateless REST APIs never face. Always establish explicit thresholds, measurement baselines, and automated monitoring.
**Architectural Leverage**: Provides predictable resource boundaries, bounds blast radius, and optimizes cost per transaction.

sections.heading: 4. Failure Modes & Trade-Offs: When to Avoid
sections.body: Improper implementation of WebSockets introduces operational bottlenecks and failure modes:
bullets: **Where to Avoid: Trade-Off Bottlenecks**: Avoid when constraints cannot tolerate: stateful connections complicate l7 load balancing, deployments, and horizontal scaling; requires custom heartbeat and reconnection logic.

**Where to Avoid: Complexity Ceiling**: Avoid when operational requirements do not justify: sse is strictly unidirectional (server -> client); long polling incurs higher http header and connection cycling overhead.
**Catastrophic Failure Modes**: Uncalibrated parameters can trigger queue exhaustion, thread starvation, cascading retry storms, and tail latency amplification.
**Operational Overhead**: Requires continuous observability (p95/p99 latency tracking, saturation alerts, and distributed tracing across hop boundaries).

sections.heading: 5. Staff+ Engineering Verdict & Interview Playbook
sections.body: Technical guidelines and evaluation criteria for WebSockets:
bullets: **Staff+ Golden Rule**: Do not default to WebSockets when communication is strictly one-way (Server -> Client): Server-Sent Events (SSE) over HTTP/2 is simpler, stateless-friendly, and handles automatic reconnection natively.

**Staff+ Interview Playbook**: Interviewers love asking: 'How do you design ChatGPT's streaming response or a live stock ticker?' If the client only listens after making one request, propose **Server-Sent Events (SSE)** over HTTP/2 instead of WebSockets: and explain why avoiding stateful bi-directional socket complexity is a win.
